Study method details: Single venipuncture with a traditional 10 ml syringe and 21-gauge needle, with blood immediately transferred into collection tubes containing either 0.105 mol buffered sodium citrate (Becton-Dickinson) or 0.129 mol buffered sodium citrate (Greiner Bio-One); caps removed and tubes filled to the nominal volume to avoid incomplete filling; tourniquet time standardised at under 30 s; a single practised phlebotomist, identical syringe and needle dimensions, and tubes of the same lot; centrifuged at 3000 g for 10 min at 10 C and plasma analysed immediately; all measurements in duplicate within a single analytical session and averaged; PT and aPTT ratios obtained using normal values calculated for the 0.105 mol concentration; paired Student t test with significance at P < 0.05; Bland-Altman analysis with differences expressed as a percentage of averages
Additional sources of bias: Tube material is confounded with citrate concentration (siliconised glass for 0.105 mol, plastic for 0.129 mol), which the authors explicitly acknowledge; PT ratio calculated using normal values established only for the 0.105 mol concentration; blood transferred from a syringe rather than drawn directly into evacuated tubes; the Table 1 caption states 20 patients while the Methods state 30
Notes: This source reports PT as a RATIO, not as an ISI-corrected INR - it is included because it is the only citrate-concentration bias figure in this project directly comparable to an INR bias, and it must not be read as an INR result. NOTABLE COINCIDENCE: the study's own desirable-bias limit (+/- 2.0%) is numerically identical to the user APS of 2%, and the reported +1.9% bias sits just inside both. The reported bias is the Bland-Altman mean of per-sample percentage differences, whereas the value calculated from the printed group means is +2.3%, which would cross the same limit - both are preserved per skill rules and the row should be treated as borderline. For context from the same table, aPTT ratio bias was +8.0% (desirable bias +/- 2.3) and fibrinogen -15.4% (desirable bias +/- 4.8), both exceeding their specifications, while D-dimer was +0.4% and unaffected. The authors hypothesise that citrate-concentration-specific reference ranges would reduce the bias.
